title: Show Codex file citations as links instead of raw markers
prompt:
Codex replies can contain file citation markers such as `:codex-file-citation{path="/abs/report.xlsx" sheet="Revenue Model" range="C27" purpose="source"}`. TerminalX shows them as raw text, on the desktop and on the phone. Show each one as a link to the file instead, labelled with its name and location, and never break one apart.

Shared parsing (packages/portable/src/codexCitations.ts, exported as `@terminalx/portable/codexCitations`):
- `matchCodexFileCitation(text)` reads a marker at the start of `text`: `{ citation, end }` or `null`. A marker is `:codex-file-citation{...}` on one line with space-separated `key=value` attributes; values are double-quoted, single-quoted or bare. `path` is required and non-empty; a path is kept exactly (spaces, Markdown punctuation, braces, backslashes, non-ASCII). Known keys map to camelCase fields: path, purpose, artifact_kind → artifactKind, sheet, range, object_id → objectId, label, page_number → pageNumber (kept as a string). Unknown keys are ignored. Anything malformed (missing path, empty path, unclosed brace or quote, a newline inside, a stray attribute without a value, square brackets, missing leading colon) is not a marker. A `javascript:` path is refused.
- `codexFileCitationName(path)`: the file name of a path or URL, percent-decoded (`file:///tmp/My%20notes.md` → `My notes.md`), including Windows paths.
- `codexFileCitationLabel(citation)`: the file name, plus " · Sheet!Range", " · Sheet" or " · p. N" when given. Google URLs are named by kind: "Google Sheets file", "Google Docs file", "Google Slides file", "Google Drive file".
- `isCodexFileOutput(citation)`: true when purpose is "output".
- `codexFileCitationParts(text)`: split plain text into `{ text }` and `{ text, citation }` parts whose texts join back to the input exactly; text without markers is one part.
- `withoutPartialCodexFileCitation(text)`: while a reply streams, hold back a trailing marker that is not finished yet (including a partial `:codex-fi` prefix), and nothing else. A marker that is closed, or ended by its line, is left as it is.

Phone (mobile/src/ui/markdown-blocks.ts): `markdownTokens` must read a marker as one inline token of type `codexFileCitation` with its `raw` text and `citation`, before emphasis or autolinks can touch the path. Markers inside inline code or code blocks stay literal; malformed ones stay text. `markdownBlocks`, which splits long paragraphs into rows, must never split a citation. Draw the token as a link in the phone's Markdown.

Desktop: render the same markers as file links in chat Markdown and in plain linked text, opening the file the way other local chat links open, and hold back a streaming marker.
notes: Modules touched by the change: packages/portable (marker parser), mobile/src (phone Markdown lexer and rows), src/lib and src/components/chat (desktop chat links and Markdown), scripts/webkit. Check: vitest, 4.3 s failing at the start, 1.3 s passing (the solution changes the lockfile, so check-task reinstalls) measured by check-task on 2026-11-12 (a fresh pnpm install adds 8 to 17 s; a cached one about 1 s). Start is the merge's first parent; solution is the merge commit.
